title: Ashtpadi 21, salok: when there was nothing
hookLine: sargun nirgun nirankaar: the Formless, with and without qualities, rested in the void (Sukhmani 21)

lines: NOT EMPTY: FULL OF WHAT'S COMING.
cards: Before a concert begins, there's a moment. The lights dim, the coughing stops, the conductor lifts the baton, and for two or three seconds a whole hall full of people holds absolutely still. It's not empty, exactly.
It's full of everything that's about to happen. Some musicians say the piece really starts there, in that silence.
The twenty-first ashtpadi of Sukhmani goes looking for the silence before the biggest piece of all: the moment before there was anything. Its word is sunn.

teach.b: The salok, in paraphrase: with qualities and without them, the Formless One was Himself absorbed in the stillness of the void. He made it all Himself, Nanak, and He Himself remembers it again.
Three words to open, and day five hundred one already met them. Sargun: with qualities, the One you can describe, near and present in the world. Nirgun: without qualities, beyond every description.
Nirankaar: the Formless. The salok says all three in one breath, and none of them cancels the others. Then sunn, which is today's word.
It comes from the Sanskrit shunya, empty.

teach.h: NOT A BLEAK NOTHING: GOD'S STILLNESS.
teach.b: But in Gurbani sunn isn't a bleak nothing. It's the deep stillness God rested in before any world existed, sunn samaadhi, absorbed in the void, the way the hall is absorbed in silence before the music.
Guru Nanak describes the same scene elsewhere, in the raag Maru: for countless ages there was only darkness, no earth, no sky, only the infinite will.

teach.h: NO DATE, NO MECHANISM: JUST WONDER.
teach.b: Gurbani doesn't try to give a date or a mechanism. It doesn't say how long, or what the stillness was like from inside.
The sources are silent there, and Sukhmani is content to leave it that way.
What it gives instead is a starting point for wonder: in Sukhmani's telling, before anything there was the One, at rest, and everything came out of that stillness.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-first ashtpadi begin with a salok picturing God, with and without qualities, resting in sunn, the stillness before creation.

o: a bleak emptiness where nothing exists
the silence kept at the end of a prayer
the stillness before creation, full of God

s: in Gurbani, sunn means a bleak, empty nothing
it's the deep stillness God rested in before creation.
the salok pictures God resting in sunn before creation
sunn samaadhi: absorbed in the stillness, like a hall before the music.
Gurbani gives a date for when creation began
it gives no date or mechanism; the sources are silent there.

games.q: the hall goes still before the music. by the salok, what was the stillness before creation?
o: a pause between two old worlds.
full: the One, absorbed in stillness.
games.why: sunn samaadhi: in Gurbani the stillness is God's own, not a bleak nothing, and the salok adds that He made it all Himself.

practice: Turn off what can be turned off, and let your eyes close or rest on the floor; you don't need to empty your mind, just stop adding to it.

Listen to the quiet underneath the small sounds, the fridge, the traffic, your own breath, and let it be like the hall before the music, full and still. If you pray, rest in Waheguru without saying anything at all.

wordCard.voice: Sunn. The stillness, or void, in which the Formless One rested before creation; from the root of the word for empty, but in Gurbani full of God.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sunn, the stillness or void before creation; from Sanskrit shunya, empty.

carryVoice: Your line: when there was nothing. In Gurbani even that stillness is full of God. That's day five hundred eighteen.
